final_claim.narrative: A single, clean time-respecting cascade carries influence from 1085 to 639. The route is 1085→359 (t=39834) → 731 (40082) → 235 (40410) → 1982 (40747) → 639 (41120), a 5-hop chain spanning only 1286 time units inside a 38400-unit window (step_01, step_03). Every hop was independently verified as a real, correctly-directed event at the stated timestamp (steps 05, 08, 09, 10, 06), so the path is not an artifact of ignoring edge direction or of aggregating repeated contacts. Inter-hop waits are 248/328/337/373, all comfortably under the 600-unit limit, and the chain still holds when the limit is tightened to 380 (step_13), showing it does not depend on the threshold being generous. Confounder controls: (a) Popularity/hub routing is ruled out — none of the relay nodes appear among the most active nodes (28, 1583, 1141, ... in step_11), and the relays are low-degree, with 5-6 events each across the whole window (step_04); within the cascade interval each relay fires only 2-3 times (step_14), so the path is a specific sequence rather than a byproduct of high-volume mixing. (b) Static connectivity alone is insufficient — restricting to [21277, 39833], where the same underlying links largely exist, yields no time-respecting route (step_12), confirming the ordering of the events is what creates the cascade. (c) Directional asymmetry: the reverse cascade 639→1085 is unreachable under identical settings, reaching only 3 nodes (step_07), which is inconsistent with a densely-mixed graph where any pair would connect by chance. The graph is sparse overall (7275 events over 1950 nodes, repeat ratio 0.026, step_02), so chance chaining is unlikely. Confidence is held below 1.0 because only one distinct route exists (step_03), making the cascade fragile to a single missing event.
